set.body:
Decision made 2026-07-28 after Project Panama and local JDK 22/25 reconnaissance.

The primary path is exact scalar restructuring before an optional, targeted Vector API artifact. The previous claim that exact-schedule axis-1 controls established an unavoidable ~0.38-0.43x scalar floor is withdrawn: directional probes showed that interleaving independent accumulators can preserve order within each 128-value block and the identical merge tree while materially increasing instruction-level parallelism. Vector API remains useful only where lanes represent independent fibers/columns and measurements beat HotSpot auto-vectorization. FFM is not a Ravel array accelerator and belongs, if needed, at a later Gale native/BLAS boundary.

Ordered plan:
1. bd-01KYN20PPYSRTGZ2NGFFTSQEZW: expand the NumPy operation/dtype/layout matrix and structural gates.
2. bd-01KYN223YR1HE8P0YP0BCTM2YJ: land exact scalar ILP reductions and remove per-element mutable dispatch/boxing.
3. bd-01KYN22457HFGK1TK11VT8QYPS: run a nonpublished targeted Vector API spike across JDK 21/25 and AArch64/x86-64.
4. bd-01KYN224B025AXR4B1C6GZSM6H: consider sumFast only with explicit user demand and a fully specified semantics contract.
5. bd-01KYN224FAK4CZ81Q8QJB3H65D: evaluate FFM only at the optional Gale native backend boundary.

Default public reductions retain the fixed 128-value block-pairwise semantics. NumPy semantic parity remains the hard gate. No Vector or FFM dependency enters ravel-core through this decision.
